2609.18736.title: Clueing up LLMs with Tool-Augmented Deductive Reasoning
2609.18736.paper_summary: Despite recent advances in large language models (LLMs), performing logically consistent deductive reasoning over extended interactions remains challenging. Tasks that require integrating evidence across multiple reasoning steps, maintaining consistency with prior inferences, and updating beliefs under new constraints can surface limitations in current models while providing a useful testbed for evaluating reasoning enhancements. In this paper, we implement a text-based, multi-agent version of the classic board game Clue as an environment to evaluate multi-step, agentic deductive reasoning. In this setting, agents must infer hidden information from a sequence of observations, maintain consistency across turns, and reason over an evolving set of logical constraints. We instantiate six LLM-based agents (GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-2.5-Flash) as players that engage in turn-based gameplay; using three agents per model family, we establish baseline performance across repeated games. We then introduce a tool-augmented approach in which a structured possibility matrix converts implicit game state from generated reasoning logs into an explicit representation of remaining possibilities. The possibility matrix encodes extended-turn memory and deductive constraints, offloading these tasks from the agent. We compare this approach against the baseline to evaluate how tool augmentation supports reasoning quality and task success for autonomous agents in a strategic reasoning environment.
2609.18736.paper_summary_zh: 儘管大型語言模型（LLMs）最近取得了進展，但在長期互動中執行邏輯一致的推理仍然具有挑戰性。需要在多個推理步驟中整合證據、保持與先前推論的一致性以及在新約束下更新信念的任務，可能會顯示出當前模型的局限性，同時提供一個有用的測試平台來評估推理的增強。在本文中，我們實現了一個基於文本的多代理版本的經典桌上遊戲 Clue，作為評估多步驟、代理性推理的環境。在這個設置中，代理必須從一系列觀察中推斷隱藏的信息，保持回合之間的一致性，並在不斷演變的邏輯約束集上進行推理。我們實例化了六個基於 LLM 的代理（GPT-4o-mini 和 Gemini-2.5-Flash）作為參與回合制遊戲的玩家；每個模型系列使用三個代理，我們在重複遊戲中建立基線性能。然後，我們引入了一種工具增強的方法，其中結構化的可能性矩陣將從生成的推理日誌中隱含的遊戲狀態轉換為剩餘可能性的明確表示。可能性矩陣編碼了擴展回合記憶和推理約束，將這些任務卸載給代理。我們將這種方法與基線進行比較，以評估工具增強如何支持自主代理在戰略推理環境中的推理質量和任務成功。
2609.18736.author: Rebecca Ansell et.al.
